question: Given $$A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0\end{bmatrix},$$ find $AB$. Hence show that the product of two non-zero matrices can be a zero matrix.
explanation:
Matrix product
$$AB=\begin{bmatrix}0(3)+(-1)(0) & 0(5)+(-1)(0) \\ 0(3)+2(0) & 0(5)+2(0)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$$
Nature of the factors
Both $A$ and $B$ contain non-zero entries, so neither matrix is a zero matrix.
Conclusion
Thus, $AB=O$ even though $A\neq O$ and $B\neq O$. Therefore, a zero matrix may be obtained as the product of two non-zero matrices.
